items.titleZh: 法拉利车手将在巴西会面讨论墨西哥首圈争斗
items.summaryZh: 法拉利车队负责人瓦塞尔将在巴西召集勒克莱尔和汉密尔顿会面，讨论两人在墨西哥首圈激烈争斗导致维斯塔潘抢走可能胜利一事。汉密尔顿坚持批评勒克莱尔，并誓言“我永远不会被噤声”。
items.originalTitle: Ferrari drivers set for crunch meeting in Brazil
items.summaryEn: Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur will bring Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton together in Brazil to discuss their costly opening-lap battle in Mexico that allowed Max Verstappen to steal a likely victory. Hamilton doubled down on his criticism of Leclerc and vowed "I'll never be silenced".
detailZh: 法拉利车队负责人弗雷德·瓦塞尔将在巴西召集他的F1车手们开会，讨论他们在墨西哥首圈代价高昂的争斗，同时刘易斯·汉密尔顿誓言“我永远不会被噤声”。
查尔斯·勒克莱尔和汉密尔顿在墨西哥首圈激烈对抗，让马克斯·维斯塔潘抢走了法拉利认为很可能到手的胜利。
汉密尔顿赛后质疑勒克莱尔的比赛技巧，称他有一种“不成功便成仁”的心态，并且长期以来对队友拼得太凶。
法拉利认为他们的争斗越界了，车队负责人瓦塞尔周日晚上对Canal+表示，这是对法拉利员工“缺乏尊重”的表现。
据《The Race》了解，瓦塞尔计划周五在巴西让汉密尔顿和勒克莱尔坐在一起讨论此事。
墨西哥站比赛结束后，瓦塞尔分别与两位车手进行了单独交谈，但他计划在巴西所有人都在同一地点时安排一次正式的面对面会谈。
勒克莱尔周三宣布他与妻子亚历山德拉的孩子出生后，缺席了巴西周四的媒体日，因此无法在巴西大奖赛周末早些时候安排会议。
由于勒克莱尔缺席，周四只有汉密尔顿面对媒体，他在会上进一步强化了对勒克莱尔的批评。
当被问及是否同意勒克莱尔对他比对其他车手更狠时，汉密尔顿以勒克莱尔在新加坡站起步阶段放弃超越马克斯·维斯塔潘为例作对比，他回答说：“是的。”
他补充道：“我可以把你们看到的说出来。新加坡站，他完全轮对轮，完全在内线，在新加坡第一弯已经抢到领先，然后收油了。
“（对他们）肯定是不一样的。如果你看看队友之间的情况，和塞巴斯蒂安（维特尔）也是这样，和卡洛斯（塞恩斯）也是这样。”
汉密尔顿明确表示，他不会改变自己直言不讳的方式，包括在车队无线电里询问勒克莱尔是否因第一圈切弯而被处罚。
“我的评论被如何看待？我不知道。我真的不在乎每个人对我所说的话有什么感受，”汉密尔顿补充道。
“我喜怒形于色，当下有什么感受就说什么。我想有一件事我希望能……我确实看到有人说过，我说的那些话是经过算计的。
“我只想用这个事实来反驳：当你在比赛中时，你的心率大约在170（次/分钟）。你以每小时200英里的速度驾驶。你没有时间去算计自己说的话，去思考自己对媒体说的话。你不会想那些。
“通常你的沮丧会向车队里的人发泄，尤其是就决策向老板们发泄。而且赛事干事也一直要求我们在有……比如说，赛道上出现问题时发声。你被耽误了，被阻挡了，他们要求你把这件事说出来。”
举个例子，如果你看墨西哥站的一节练习赛，[伊萨克] 哈贾尔在1号弯的赛车线上减速让行，我当时什么都没说。他们也没有调查。如果当时我开口了，比如举起双手示意，他们就会调查，他就会因为阻挡而受罚。
所以重要的是确保自己保持开放。当然，有时候你说了些话，事后可能会后悔，但我不会。我永远不会为做真实、真诚的自己而道歉。我永远不会被噤声。
没有人要求我什么都不要说。事情就是这样。
汉密尔顿表示，他“非常努力地与夏尔建立良好的关系”，因为他知道勒克莱尔在为法拉利效力八年后“已经深深融入了车队”。
“我一直努力保持尊重，”汉密尔顿说。
“自然，像我这样的人加入一支车队并不容易，因为我非常直言不讳，我不断推动、推动、再推动，推动如此多的改变。而且我还会推动更多。只要我在这里，就会是这样。我来这里是为了赢。为了能够赢，你必须与身边的每个人合作。”
汉密尔顿坚称他“完全理解自己对车队的责任”，并表示他“一直努力表达对他们的感激，并竭尽全力帮助推动车队前进，我觉得自己是车队今天所处位置的重要一部分，这是积极的”。
他说他们“还没有时间坐下来全部面对面交流，因为弗雷德回到了马拉内罗，查尔斯回到了摩纳哥。
“但我们会坐下来谈一谈。我不认为所有问题都能在一次会议里解决。但这很重要。”
“我们现在打造的东西会让我们在明年处于正确的位置。从某些方面来说，我很高兴我们有过那样的经历。当然，我更希望赢下比赛并拿到一二名。但从那之中，你可以学到东西。”
“我真的相信明年我们能够为世界冠军而战。这是唯一的目标。所以现在，在幕后，我的重点是继续保持在最近几场比赛中在执行方面所取得的性能表现，然后致力于明年的赛车。”
“显然，除了推动他们之外，我对引擎无能为力，而他们会继续在幕后推动，我相信他们正在这样做。至于赛车，就是驾驭它，确保我们把它引向正确的方向。确保我们以正确的姿态迎接明年。然后弗雷德的工作就是确保我们所有人都朝着同一个方向前进。”
“当然，我们会奋力比赛。但要公平，并确保我们从中获得最大收益。”
汉密尔顿支持瓦塞尔，表示“我仍然相信弗雷德是带领我们夺得冠军的合适人选”。
当被问及他接下来想要什么时：“我认为关键在于沟通。关键在于理解。
“我还不太清楚。我试着想象过会议会是什么样子，会如何进行。我从来都不知道。”
“但我会做的是，确保我始终做真实的自己。对于我参与的任何部分以及我为车队做出的任何决定，我都不会回避责任。并且会继续努力推进。”
detailEn: Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur will get his Formula 1 drivers together in Brazil to discuss their costly opening-lap dice in Mexico, as Lewis Hamilton vows "I'll never be silenced".
Charles Leclerc and Hamilton fought each other hard on the opening lap in Mexico, allowing Max Verstappen to steal away what Ferrari believed was a likely victory.
Hamilton called into question Leclerc's racecraft after the race, saying he has a "do or die" mentality and a long history of fighting his team-mates too hard.
Ferrari felt that their battle crossed a line with team boss Vasseur telling Canal+ on Sunday evening that it was evidence of a "lack of respect" to Ferrari's employees.
The Race understands Vasseur is planning to sit Hamilton and Leclerc down together on Friday in Brazil to discuss the matter.
Vasseur spoke to both drivers individually after the race in Mexico, but he's planned a proper sit-down for Brazil when they're all in the same place.
Leclerc missed Thursday media day in Brazil after announcing the birth of his and his wife Alexandra's child on Wednesday, so a meeting earlier in the Brazil weekend wasn't possible.
With Leclerc absent, only Hamilton faced the media on Thursday, where he doubled down on his criticism of Leclerc.

Asked whether he agreed that Leclerc races him harder than other drivers, with the example of Leclerc backing out of passing Max Verstappen at the start in Singapore used as a comparison, Hamilton replied "Yes."
He added: "I can say what you see. Singapore, he was fully wheel to wheel, fully on the inside, had won the lead in Turn 1 in Singapore and backed off.
"Definitely [races them] different. If you look at the team-mates, it's the same with Sebastian [Vettel], it's the same with Carlos [Sainz]."
Hamilton made it clear he isn't going to change his outspoken approach, including over the team radio when he was asking if Leclerc had been penalised on lap one for cutting the track.
"How have my comments have been taken? I don't know. I don't really care how everyone feels about what I've said," Hamilton added.

"I wear my heart on my sleeve and I say how I feel in the moment. I think one thing that I would like to...I did see something that someone was saying that it's calculated, the things that I'm saying.

"I just want to combat that with the fact that when you're in the race, your heart rate is like 170[beats per minute]. You're driving at 200 miles an hour. You don't have time to be calculating what you're saying and thinking [what] you're saying to the media. You don't think about that.

"Usually your frustration comes out towards the people in the team, particularly the bosses about decisions. And also the stewards have always asked us to voice when we have…If there's an issue on the track, for example. You get held up, you get blocked, they ask you to voice it.

"An example is, if you look in Mexico, one of the practice sessions, [Isack] Hadjar, backed off on the racing line into Turn 1, I didn't say anything. They didn't look into it. If I had spoken, like throwing my hands up, for example, they would have investigated and he would have got a penalty, because it was impeding.

"So it is important to make sure you're open. Of course, there's some times you say things and maybe you might regret it afterwards, but I don't. I'm never going to apologise for being authentic and real. I'm never going to be silenced.
"I've not been asked to not say anything. And that's just the way it is."
Hamilton says he's "really worked hard to build a good relationship with Charles", knowing Leclerc is "very much embedded within the team" after eight years driving for Ferrari.
"I've always tried to be respectful," Hamilton said.

"Naturally, it's not so easy having someone like me come into a team because I'm very outspoken and I push and push and push, push for so many changes. And I'm going to be pushing for more. And as long as I'm here, that's how it's going to be. I'm here to win. To be able to win, you have to work with everyone around you."

Hamilton insists he "fully understands my responsibility to the team" and said he's "always trying to show my appreciation for them and my absolute utmost to help push the team forwards and I feel like I've been a big part of where we are today as a team, which is positive".
He said they "haven't had a time to sit down all face-to-face because Fred's been back in Maranello and Charles has been back in Monaco.
"But we will have a sit-down. I don't think everything's going to get squashed and sorted out in one meeting. But it is important.
"What we build now will put us in the right position for next year. And in some ways, I'm glad we've had that experience. Of course I'd rather have won and had a 1-2. But from that, you can learn.

"I really do believe that next year we can be fighting for world championships. That is the sole goal. So right now, in the background, my focus is on continuing to hold on to the performance we've picked up in the last few races in terms of execution and then working on next year's car.

"I obviously can't do anything about the engine, except for just push them and they'll continue to push in the background, I believe they are. With the car, it's steering it, making sure we steer it in the right direction. Making sure we arrive next year on the right foot. Then Fred's job is to make sure that we are all in the same direction.
"Of course, we're going to race hard. But fair and making sure that we get the maximum out of it."
Hamilton backed Vasseur, saying "I still believe Fred is the right guy to lead us to the championship".
Asked what he wants moving forward: "I think it's about communication. It's about understanding.
"I don't really know yet. I've tried to think of what the meeting will be like, how it's going to go. I never ever know.

"But what I will do is I'll make sure I'm always just authentically me. I won't back down from taking responsibility for any part that I play and any decisions that I make for the team. And just continue to push."
keyPointsZh: 瓦塞尔赛后对Canal+表示，两人的争斗是对法拉利员工“缺乏尊重”的表现。
瓦塞尔在墨西哥赛后已分别与两位车手谈话，但计划在巴西三人同处时正式坐下来讨论。
勒克莱尔因周三宣布孩子出生而缺席巴西周四媒体日，因此无法更早会面。
keyPointsEn: Vasseur told Canal+ after the race that their battle was evidence of a "lack of respect" to Ferrari's employees.
Vasseur spoke to both drivers individually after Mexico but planned a proper sit-down in Brazil when all three are in the same place.
Leclerc missed Thursday media day in Brazil after announcing the birth of his child on Wednesday, so an earlier meeting in Brazil wasn't possible.

items.originalTitle: Lewis Hamilton admits his outspoken nature has made Ferrari move more difficult
detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿承认他的直言不讳使得在法拉利与查尔斯·勒克莱尔相处更加困难
刘易斯·汉密尔顿已经承认他的直言不讳使得他在法拉利与查尔斯·勒克莱尔一起融入更加困难，他解释说：“像我这样的人加入一个车队并不那么容易。”
对于法拉利车迷来说，这是最新的Scuderia 法拉利 F1新闻，包括来自马拉内洛以及更远地方的赛车手更新、技术分析和比赛反应。
七届一级方程式赛车冠军刘易斯·汉密尔顿承认他的直言不讳使得他在法拉利与查尔斯·勒克莱尔一起融入更加困难，解释说：“像我这样的人加入一个车队并不那么容易。”
汉密尔顿在2025赛季初加入了马拉内洛车队，在上周末的墨西哥大奖赛的首圈与勒克莱尔发生了碰撞。
勒克莱尔试图超越从杆位起步的汉密尔顿，但两位车手都冲出了赛道。因此，汉密尔顿从第一跌至第三，排在维斯塔潘之后，勒克莱尔被处以5秒罚时。
在墨西哥城的赛后新闻发布会上，这位英国人呼吁团队内部进行"严肃的谈话"，并在巴西再次谈到了这一情况。
当被问及勒克莱尔与法拉利的长期关系是否让他更难融入车队时，汉密尔顿说："他来这里已经很久了。八年的时间里，他为车队赢得了九次胜利。他在车队中根深蒂固，我知道这始终是一个挑战。"
“我一直都很尊重这一点，我努力与车队建立良好的关系，与查尔斯建立联系，弥合差距，确保我们和谐共处，共同努力。我一直都试图保持尊重。”
他解释了他为什么认为他加入法拉利的到来总会让车队中的一些人感到谨慎。
当然，像我这样的人加入一个团队并不容易，因为我非常直言不讳，我不断推动，不断推动。我推动了许多改变，”他补充说。“我还会继续推动更多。只要我还在这里，事情就会是这样。
我来这里是为了赢得比赛，为了能够赢得比赛，你必须与周围的人一起工作。你必须推动，我也必须推动。我也需要被推动才能提升。我们都可以不断提升，变得更好，我真心相信这个车队明年可以为了冠军而战。”
detailEn: Lewis Hamilton admits his outspoken nature has made Ferrari move more difficult
Lewis Hamilton has admitted that his outspoken approach has made it harder to integrate at Ferrari alongside Charles Leclerc
For Ferrari fans. The latest Scuderia Ferrari F1 news, driver updates, technical analysis and race reaction from Maranello and beyond.

Seven-time Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton has admitted that his outspoken approach has made it harder for him to fit in at Ferrari alongside Charles Leclerc, explaining that "it’s not so easy having someone like me come into a team."
Hamilton, who joined the Maranello outfit at the start of the 2025 season, clashed with Leclerc on the opening lap of last weekend's Mexican Grand Prix.

Leclerc attempted to overtake Hamilton, who started from pole position, but both drivers ran off the track. Hamilton dropped from first to third behind Max Verstappen as a result, and Leclerc was handed a five-second penalty.
While speaking to the media after the race in Mexico City, the Briton called for "serious talks" within the team and has now spoken about the situation again in Brazil.

"He’s been here a long time," Hamilton said when asked whether Leclerc's long-standing relationship with Ferrari had made it harder for him to settle into the team. "Eight years and had nine wins with the team. He is very much embedded within the team, and I know that it would always be a challenge.

"I’ve always respected that, and I’ve approached the team and really worked hard to build a good relationship with Charles and bridge the gap and make sure that we’re harmonious and work hard together. Always tried to be respectful."
He explained why he believes his arrival at Ferrari was always going to make some within the team cautious.

"Naturally, it’s not so easy having someone like me come into a team, because I’m very outspoken and I push and push and push. Push for so many changes," he added. "And I’m going to be pushing for more. And as long as I’m here, that’s how it’s going to be.

"I’m here to win, and to be able to win, you have to work with everyone around you. You have to push, and I have to push. I have to be pushed also to elevate. We can all always elevate and be better, and I truly believe that this team can be fighting for the championship next year."

拉尔夫·舒马赫抨击刘易斯·汉密尔顿表现得像“卡彭”并在无线电中对法拉利维修区进行威胁，
对于法拉利车迷来说，这是最新的Scuderia 法拉利 F1新闻，车手更新，技术分析和来自马拉内洛及更远地方的赛事反应，
刘易斯·汉密尔顿在墨西哥城大奖赛期间的愤怒无线电信息遭到了前一级方程式车手拉尔夫·舒马赫的严厉批评。
尽管法拉利车队队友在阿维莫多罗·赫尔曼诺斯·罗德里格斯赛道上的碰撞被视为可接受的激烈赛车，但随后在无线电波中的政治戏剧对德国评论员来说已经越过了重大界限。
汉密尔顿和查尔斯·勒克莱尔在比赛的起步阶段就展开了激烈的对抗，最终迫使两辆红色赛车在4号弯完全脱离赛道。而不是屈服，摩纳哥车手将脚踩在草地上以捍卫自己的赛道位置，因此受到了国际汽联五秒的处罚。
在接受天空体育德国采访时，舒马赫将这次身体冲突视为常规程序。
'刘易斯·汉密尔顿已经接受，如果查尔斯·勒克莱尔不穿过草地驾驶，就会发生碰撞，'这位51岁的老将解释说，这次挤压完全是故意的。'但我对此没有问题，因为这是一种赛车情况，每个人都不想放弃自己的位置。'
六次大奖赛冠军感到愤怒的是事件立即的后果。对于4号弯道的挤压，这位英国明星立刻跳上无线电要求赛事控制对他在车队的队友进行处罚。
当维修区墙壁试图管理局势时，这位经验丰富的车手升级了紧张局势，向马拉内洛车队高层发出了一个含蓄的警告。
“我对随后发生的戏剧性事件有意见，”舒马赫反驳道，“你不能在无线电上要求对你的队友进行处罚。”
查尔斯·勒克莱尔，法拉利，刘易斯·汉密尔顿，法拉利
天空体育分析师对投诉的语气特别震惊，指责这位41岁的车手完全不尊重车队的管理层。
"然后像阿尔·卡彭一样说话并威胁说‘我们有大问题’——在我看来，狗在遛主人," �舒马赫严厉地说。
马拉内洛的领导危机？
‘狗在遛主人’的残酷评论凸显了意大利车队内部日益加剧的权力斗争。随着这位超级车手积极制定条款并在直播中公开威胁维修区，舒马赫认为车队负责人弗雷德·瓦瑟尔正在迅速失去对明星车队的控制。
查尔斯·勒克莱尔，法拉利，刘易斯·汉密尔顿，法拉利
随着车队内部的竞争威胁到可能影响车队进入巴西的势头，这位前F1车手要求管理层立即干预，以重新建立清晰的等级制度。
"现在必须立即做出改变，"他警告说。
detailEn: Ralf Schumacher accuses Lewis Hamilton of acting like “Al Capone” amid Mexico City GP drama
Ralf Schumacher slams Lewis Hamilton for acting like "Al Capone" and threatening the Ferrari pitwall over the radio
For Ferrari fans. The latest Scuderia Ferrari F1 news, driver updates, technical analysis and race reaction from Maranello and beyond.
Lewis Hamilton’s furious radio messages during the Mexico City Grand Prix have drawn severe criticism from former Formula 1 driver Ralf Schumacher.

While the clash between the Ferrari team-mates at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez was deemed acceptable hard racing, the ensuing political theatre over the airwaves crossed a major line for the German pundit.

Hamilton and Charles Leclerc went to war through the opening sequence of corners, ultimately forcing both scarlet cars completely off the asphalt at Turn 4. Rather than yielding, the Monegasque driver kept his foot planted across the grass to defend his track position, earning a five-second time penalty from the FIA in the process.
Speaking to Sky Sports Germany, Schumacher brushed off the physical altercation as standard procedure.

"Lewis Hamilton has accepted that if Charles Leclerc doesn’t drive across the meadow, a crash will occur," the 51-year-old explained, noting the squeeze was entirely intentional. "But I have no problem with that, because it’s a racing situation where everyone doesn’t want to give up their position."

What infuriated the six-time Grand Prix winner was the immediate aftermath. Furious over the Turn 4 squeeze, the British star immediately jumped on the radio to demand race control penalise his own garage mate.
When the pitwall attempted to manage the situation, the veteran driver escalated the tension, delivering a thinly veiled warning to the Maranello brass.
"What I have a problem with is the drama that followed," Schumacher fired back. "You don’t demand a penalty for your team-mate over the radio."
Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari
The Sky Sports analyst was particularly appalled by the tone of the complaints, accusing the 41-year-old of completely disrespecting the team's authority.
"Then to speak like Al Capone and threaten that ‘we have big, big problems’—from my point of view, the dog is walking the owner," Schumacher slammed.
A leadership crisis at Maranello?

The brutal "dog is walking the owner" comment highlights a growing power struggle within the Italian garage. With the superstar driver actively dictating terms and publicly threatening the pitwall during a live broadcast, Schumacher believes team principal Fred Vasseur is rapidly losing control of his blockbuster line-up.
Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari

As the intra-team rivalry threatens to potentially affect the squad's momentum heading into Brazil, the former F1 driver demanded immediate intervention from the executives to re-establish a clear hierarchy.
"Something urgently needs to be changed now," he warned.

items.originalTitle: Max Verstappen jokes about rain threat in Brazil: "I've installed antivirus now!"
items.summaryEn: When asked whether he fears a repeat of the power unit software bug seen in Malaysia during a possible wet race in Brazil, Verstappen joked: "I've installed antivirus now!"
detailZh: 维斯塔潘调侃巴西雨战威胁：“我现在已经装好杀毒软件了！”
F1车手在巴西可能再次遭遇降雨，不过当被问及是否担心马来西亚站动力单元软件故障重演时，维斯塔潘以玩笑回应。
2026款F1赛车的首场雨战并未取得圆满成功。在雪邦国际赛道安全车带领下的编队圈中，近半数赛车停了下来。
问题最终被认定为与软件故障有关，该故障与国际汽联为雨战设定的250千瓦限制相关。这一软件故障导致电机在赛道最慢路段进入锁定模式。由于没有电力来弥补涡轮迟滞，车手踩下油门踏板时毫无反应。
在马来西亚，针对问题最严重的迷你赛段，限制被解除，国际汽联在大约20分钟后向各车队和制造商发送了新软件。随后，他们得以在动力单元中安装更新版本，最终让比赛得以开始。
同样的紧急措施随后在新加坡实施，之后在奥斯汀进行了修改版软件的测试。在美洲赛道，国际汽联发表了以下声明：
“作为对低抓地力模式动力单元软件持续改进的一部分，国际汽联将与各车队和动力单元制造商一起，在第一节自由练习结束后进行模拟，赛车将处于低抓地力模式，在回场圈使用特定的车手输入来测试额外的软件保护措施。这意味着赛车将在本节练习结束时在15号弯以低速行驶一小段距离。”
国际汽联单座赛车总监尼古拉斯·通巴西斯此前已在马来西亚解释，该漏洞只是在比赛中才暴露出来，因为国际汽联此前无法在湿地条件下对2026款赛车进行足够的测试。在回答Motorsport.com的提问时，他确认可以保证这一特定漏洞不会再次发生，不过他补充说，他无法排除所有漏洞。
鉴于圣保罗的天气预报，本周末F1车手有可能再次遇到降雨。在国际汽联新闻发布会上被问及车手们是否有信心雪邦的混乱不会重演时，马克斯·维斯塔潘开玩笑说：“我给赛车装了杀毒软件，所以我没事！”
当小红牛车手阿维德·林德布拉德随后表示希望问题已经解决时，维斯塔潘再次拿起麦克风笑道：“伙计，你用的也是同一套软件，所以别担心！”
维斯塔潘对英特拉格斯在干地和湿地条件下都留有美好回忆。这位红牛车手曾三次在此夺冠，并同样三次上演令人难忘的逆转驾驶。
去年，这位荷兰车手从维修区起步一路登上领奖台；2024年他从第17位发车夺冠——当时对兰多·诺里斯的争冠希望造成了决定性打击；2016年他奉献了一场精彩表演，包括在雨中从外道超越最终的世界冠军尼科·罗斯伯格。
“这是一条很棒的赛道，很适合比赛，”维斯塔潘说。“而且没错，它有时候上演过一些疯狂的正赛，对我来说也是如此。无论是从前面起步赢下比赛，还是像雨战之类的情况从后面追上来获胜。看起来这次又有可能下雨，所以那很令人兴奋。”
不过，维斯塔潘不愿对今年的比赛做出任何预测。尽管这位红牛车手赢下了最近四场大奖赛中的三场，他总结说，四支领先车队实力非常接近，而法拉利在奥斯汀拥有最快的赛车配置。
“这个周末很难说什么，因为我认为前面的差距太小了，有时候就取决于把赛车调校或能量部署做到位，诸如此类的事情。
“过去几年，我认为巴西一直是冲刺赛周末。所以现在我想我们多了一点时间来调校赛车，这可能是好事也可能是坏事。我不知道，但我们拭目以待吧。”
detailEn: Max Verstappen jokes about rain threat in Brazil: "I've installed antivirus now!"
F1 drivers could once again face rain in Brazil, although Verstappen responds with a joke when asked whether he fears a repeat of the power unit software bug seen in Malaysia

The first wet race with Formula 1’s 2026 cars did not exactly prove to be a resounding success. During the formation laps behind the safety car at the Sepang International Circuit, almost half the field came to a halt.

The issue turned out to be a software bug linked to the 250kW restrictions imposed by the FIA for wet-weather races. That software bug caused the electric motors to go into lock-down mode in the slowest parts of the circuit. With no electric power available to offset the turbo lag, nothing happened when the drivers pressed the throttle pedal.

In Malaysia, the restrictions were lifted for the most problematic minisectors, with the FIA sending new software to the teams and manufacturers after approximately 20 minutes. They were then able to install the updated version in their power units to finally get the race under way.
The same emergency measure was subsequently applied in Singapore, before a test with modified software followed in Austin. At the Circuit of the Americas, the FIA issued the following statement:

"As part of the ongoing refinements to the Power Unit software for low grip mode, the FIA together with the teams and Power Unit manufacturers will run a simulation at the end of FP1, with cars running on low grip mode, using specific driver inputs during the in-lap to test additional software protections. This will mean that cars will be running for a short distance at low speed at Turn 15 at the end of the session."

FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis had already explained in Malaysia that the bug had only come to light during the race because the FIA had not been able to carry out sufficient testing with the 2026 cars in wet conditions beforehand. In response to a question from Motorsport.com, he confirmed that he could guarantee this specific bug would not occur again, although he added that he could not rule out all bugs.

Given the weather forecast for Sao Paulo, there is a possibility that F1 drivers will once again encounter rain this weekend. Asked during the FIA press conference whether the drivers are confident that the Sepang debacle will not be repeated, Max Verstappen joked: "I have installed antivirus in my car, so I'll be fine!"

When Racing Bulls driver Arvid Lindblad then said that he hoped the issue had been resolved, Verstappen picked up the microphone once more and laughed: "You'll be on the same software, mate, so don't worry!"
Verstappen has fond memories of Interlagos in both dry and wet conditions. The Red Bull driver has won there three times and has produced memorable comeback drives on just as many occasions.

Last year, the Dutchman drove from the pitlane to the podium, while in 2024 he managed to win from 17th on the grid – which at the time dealt a decisive blow to Lando Norris's title hopes – and in 2016 he put on a spectacular show, including overtaking eventual world champion Nico Rosberg around the outside in the rain.

"It's a fantastic track and good for racing", Verstappen said. "And yeah, it has had some crazy races at times, also for me. Winning from starting up front or winning after coming from the back with rain races and stuff like that. It's looking like there’s a chance of rain again, so that’s exciting."

However, Verstappen is reluctant to make any predictions for this year's edition. Although the Red Bull driver has won three of the last four Grands Prix, he concluded that the four leading teams are very closely matched and that Ferrari had the fastest package in Austin.
"It's difficult to say anything for this weekend, because I think the gaps are so tight up front that sometimes it just comes down to nailing the setup or the deployment, all these kind of things.

"The last few years, I think Brazil has always been a sprint event. So now I guess we have a little bit more time to set up the car, which might be good or might be bad. I don't know, but we'll just see how it goes."

items.originalTitle: Lewis Hamilton backs claims Charles Leclerc races him harder than F1 rivals
items.summaryEn: Lewis Hamilton believes Ferrari needs further talks to clarify its rules of engagement, and backs claims that Charles Leclerc races him harder than drivers from rival teams.
detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿支持勒克莱尔比F1对手车手对他拼得更凶的说法
墨西哥F1站与队友查尔斯·勒克莱尔发生冲突一周后，刘易斯·汉密尔顿坚持认为需要进一步沟通，以避免伤害法拉利
刘易斯·汉密尔顿坚持认为法拉利需要进一步沟通以明确交战规则，并支持勒克莱尔比对手车队的车手对他拼得更凶的说法。
上周末墨西哥站第一圈，汉密尔顿与勒克莱尔发生碰撞，两人在4号弯双双冲出赛道，这最终给了马克斯·维斯塔潘绝佳的夺冠机会，也让法拉利错失了可能的1-2名胜利，两人最终分列第二和第四。
汉密尔顿对勒克莱尔在首圈如此激烈地缠斗感到愤怒，而这位摩纳哥车手却在4号弯切弯后永久保持领先。勒克莱尔仅因获得持久优势而被罚五秒，减轻处罚因素使这一惩罚从10秒降至5秒。
他们在墨西哥的较量进一步印证了勒克莱尔似乎比任何人都更激烈地与队友竞争的说法，此前在新加坡大奖赛中，勒克莱尔尽管完全处于杆位得主马克斯·维斯塔潘的内侧，却在起步时退让了。然而，勒克莱尔在随后奥斯汀的美国大奖赛中确实与这位荷兰车手激烈缠斗，在COTA的S弯外侧超越了红牛车手。
当被问及勒克莱尔比其他车手更激烈地与他竞争这一看法是否也是汉密尔顿所注意到的，这位七届世界冠军回答道：“是的。我看到的和你看到的一样。在新加坡，他完全处于1号弯的内侧，他已经赢得了领先，然后他退让了。这确实不同。
“但我的意思是，如果你看看队友们，和塞巴斯蒂安（维特尔）也是一样。和卡洛斯（塞恩斯）也是一样。
情绪高涨之际，汉密尔顿要求进行对话以明确车队的交战规则，并警告车队将面临“大问题”。Motorsport.com了解到，车队领队弗雷德里克·瓦塞尔在认为墨西哥站的事件显示出对车队2000名员工缺乏尊重后，已分别与两位车手进行了简短交谈。
但由于瓦塞尔在比赛间隙已返回欧洲，而勒克莱尔在女儿出生后与家人共度时光，汉密尔顿表示仍需进一步对话。
当被Motorsport.com问及在冷静下来后是否对墨西哥站事件有了不同看法时，他说：“我自然感到沮丧，现在仍然沮丧。所以，需要进行对话。我们会在时间允许时进行这些对话。”
“我们曾有机会为车队赢得胜利。车队今年在带来升级方面做得非常出色，我认为他们完成了令人难以置信的工作。在过去三四场比赛中，我们获得的积分比任何其他车队都多。我们本可以轻松实现一二名完赛，所以我们绝对必须努力确保这种情况不再发生。”
汉密尔顿也因公开游说让队友受到比维修区停留五秒更重的处罚而受到批评，因为在超车极为困难的赛道上，切弯给勒克莱尔带来的优势远大于五秒罚时。
但这位41岁的车手表示他“不会被噤声”。“我真的不在乎大家对我所说的话有什么感受。我坦率直白，想到什么就说什么，”他说。
“我确实看到有人说我说的话是经过算计的，我想用这样一个事实来反驳：当你在比赛中时，你的心率大约在170。你以每小时200英里的速度驾驶。你根本没有时间去算计自己说的话，也没时间去想媒体会怎么写，你不会想这些。
“当然，有时候你说了一些话，事后可能会后悔，但我不会，我永远不会为做真实、真诚的自己而道歉。我不会被噤声。我从来、从来没有被噤声过。没有人（车队）要求我不要说任何话，事情就是这样。”
detailEn: Lewis Hamilton backs claims Charles Leclerc races him harder than F1 rivals
One week on from his Mexico Formula 1 clash with team-mate Charles Leclerc, Lewis Hamilton maintains further talks are needed to avoid hurting Ferrari
Lewis Hamilton maintains Ferrari needs further talks to iron out its rules of engagement, backing claims Charles Leclerc races him harder than drivers from rival teams.

Hamilton and Leclerc came to blows on lap one of last weekend's race in Mexico with both drivers going off the track at Turn 4, which eventually handed Max Verstappen a golden opportunity to snatch away the win and costing Ferrari a possible 1-2 victory, instead the duo finishing second and fourth.

Hamilton was incensed by how hard Leclerc raced on the opening lap, only for the Monegasque to permanently stay ahead as he cut the track at Turn 4. Leclerc only received a five-second penalty for gaining a lasting advantage, with mitigation bringing that punishment down from 10 seconds.

Their Mexico fight further fed suggestions that Leclerc appears to race his teammate harder than anyone else, having come after a Singapore Grand Prix in which Leclerc backed off at the start despite being fully on the inside of polesitter Max Verstappen. Leclerc did race the Dutchman hard at the subsequent US Grand Prix in Austin, however, overtaking the Red Bull man around the outside of COTA's Esses.

When asked if the idea of Leclerc racing him harder than other drivers is something Hamilton has also noticed, the seven-time world champion replied: "Yes. I see what you see. In Singapore, he was fully on the inside into Turn 1, he had won the lead, and he backed off. It was definitely different.
"But I mean, if you look at the team-mates, it was the same with Sebastian [Vettel]. It was the same with Carlos [Sainz].

As emotions ran high, Hamilton demanded talks to clarify the team's rules of engagement and warned of "big problems" for the squad. Motorsport.com understands team principal Fred Vasseur has spoken briefly to both drivers, albeit separately, after feeling the events of Mexico showed a lack of respect towards the team's 2000 people staff.
But with Vasseur having travelled back to Europe in between races and Leclerc spending time with his family following the birth of his daughter, Hamilton says further talks are still needed.

"Naturally I was frustrated, and I'm still frustrated," he said when asked by Motorsport.com if he views the events of Mexico in a different light now they have had time to cool off. "So, conversations need to be had. We will have those when the time permits.

"We had an opportunity to win for the team. The team has done such an amazing job in bringing upgrades this year and I think they've done an incredible job. We've scored more points than any other team in the last three or four races. We could have easily had a one-two, so we definitely have to work towards making sure that doesn't happen again."

Hamilton drew criticism, too, for openly lobbying for his team-mate to get a bigger penalty than the five seconds he was held at his pitstop, as cutting the track handed Leclerc a much bigger advantage than that on a circuit where overtaking proved extremely difficult.
But the 41-year-old said he "will not be silenced". "I don't really care how everyone feels about what I've said. I wear my heart on my sleeve, and I say how I feel in the moment," he said.

"I did see something that someone was saying that the things that I'm saying are calculated, and I just want to combat that with the fact that when you're in the race, your heart rate is like 170. You're driving 200 miles an hour. You don't have time to be calculated in what you're saying and thinking about what the media are going to write about, you don't think about that.

"Of course, there's some times you say things and maybe you might regret it afterwards, but I don't, and I'm never going to apologise for being authentic and real. I'm not gonna be silenced. I've never ever been silenced. I have not been asked to not say anything [by the team], and that's just the way it is."

items.summaryZh: 随着IndyCar系列赛准备前往巴塞罗那举行国际展示，车手们对将美国开放式赛车锦标赛进一步推向海外的热情正在增加。墨西哥IndyCar赛事的可能性一直是车队的热门话题。

items.originalTitle: Colton Herta backs Mexico IndyCar race following Pato O’Ward promoter callout
detailZh: 科顿·赫塔在帕托·奥瓦尔呼吁墨西哥IndyCar赛事后表示支持
与奥瓦尔呼吁对有激情的股东承诺一致，凯迪拉克F1的测试车手表示强烈支持将美国开放式赛车锦标赛进一步向南推进
科顿·赫塔在墨西哥大奖赛的第一节自由练习中代表凯迪拉克赛车队
随着IndyCar系列赛准备前往海外，为刚刚宣布的国际展示活动在巴塞罗那做准备，将美国开放式赛车锦标赛进一步推向海外的热情正在积聚力量 - 尤其是车手们自己。

墨西哥未来举办IndyCar赛事的可能性一直是车队的热门话题，来自蒙特雷的Arrow 迈凯伦车队的Pato O'Ward作为这项运动最受欢迎的车手，处于风口浪尖。在墨西哥F1赛事期间巴塞罗那赛事确认之后，O'Ward再次表达了他对当地利益相关者的持续不满，指出阻碍他在家乡举办赛事的宣传障碍。他之前已经指出区域组织者缺乏真正的渴望和承诺，O'Ward警告说，任何在墨西哥的潜在活动都需要那些真正热衷于发展这项运动而不是仅仅寻找快速赚钱的利益相关者。
当被问及尽管有这些宣传障碍，IndyCar能否在墨西哥成功时，九次IndyCar赛事冠军和当前凯迪拉克 F1测试车手Colton Herta对这一想法表示了坚决的支持，突出了O'Ward的明星魅力和赛道独特的技术要求。
“百分之百。”Herta说，“我认为它可以同样受欢迎。其中一个重要原因是Pato和他的受欢迎程度。我认为这里的赛车将会非常精彩。我认为看到IndyCar在这条赛道上的表现将会非常有趣。特别是考虑到赛道的护栏和护栏轮廓。在IndyCar中，你通常可以对护栏采取比在F1中更激进的态度。”

Herta，26岁，有着独特的视角。尽管他与美国的开放式赛车场景紧密相连，在IndyCar中已经完成了七个全职赛季，但这位加利福尼亚州本土人本赛季一直在努力缩短与欧洲的差距——在Hitech的Formula 2中与凯迪拉克的F1项目角色并行竞争。在墨西哥城第五次FP1亮相之后，Herta本周末将在Interlagos进行他今年的第六次周五练习，以获得他长期追求的FIA超级驾照参加F1赛事所需的最后一点积分。
进一步思考开放式赛车在国际上的发展趋势以及新增加的巴塞罗那赛事日期，赫塔总结道：
“我认为这将是一场精彩的比赛。我认为巴塞罗那是件很酷的事情。我认为如果他们能在这里举办比赛那就更酷了。”
detailEn: Colton Herta backs Mexico IndyCar race following Pato O’Ward promoter callout
Echoing O'Ward's call for passionate stakeholder commitment, Cadillac F1’s test driver voices strong support for taking the American open-wheel championship further south
Colton Herta, with Cadillac Racing during FP1 of the Mexico Grand Prix.

As the IndyCar Series prepares to head overseas for its newly announced international showcase in Barcelona, enthusiasm for taking the American open-wheel championship even further abroad is gathering momentum - especially among the drivers themselves.

The prospect of a future IndyCar round in Mexico has long been a hot topic in the paddock, with Arrow McLaren’s Pato O’Ward, a native of Monterrey, front and center as the sport’s most popular driver. Speaking after the Barcelona race confirmation during the F1 round in Mexico, O'Ward renewed his ongoing frustrations with local stakeholders, noting the promotional roadblocks that have stalled a race in his home country. Having previously flagged a lack of genuine hunger and commitment among regional organizers, O'Ward warned that any prospective event in Mexico would require stakeholders who are genuinely passionate about building the sport rather than simply looking for a quick payday.

When asked whether IndyCar could succeed in Mexico despite those promotional hurdles, nine-time IndyCar race winner and current Cadillac F1 test driver Colton Herta voiced resounding support for the idea, highlighting O'Ward's star power and the unique technical demands of the track.

“A thousand percent.” Herta said. “I think it could be just as popular. A big reason for that is Pato and his popularity here. I think the racing would be incredible here. I think it would be very interesting to see what an IndyCar could do around this track. Especially with the curbing and the curb profiles. With the IndyCar you can typically be a lot more aggressive with the curbs than in the Formula 1.”

Herta, 26, speaks from a unique vantage point. Though deeply tied to the American open-wheel scene with seven full-time seasons in IndyCar, the California native has spent the season bridging the gap to Europe – competing in Formula 2 with Hitech alongside his role with Cadillac’s F1 program. Fresh off his fifth FP1 appearance in Mexico City, Herta is slated for his sixth Friday practice outing of the year at Interlagos this weekend to attain the final point necessary for his long-pursued FIA Superlicense to race in F1.
Reflecting further on the broader international trajectory of open-wheel racing and the newly minted Barcelona date, Herta concluded:
“I think it would put on a great show. I think Barcelona is a really cool thing. I think it would be cool if they could follow it up with the race here.”
